title: Give Yourself Permission to Make Bad Drafts
description: The first version is supposed to be rough. Letting it be rough is what allows a second version to exist.

body.heading: The draft is not the thing
paragraphs: Almost everything good you have ever read, watched or listened to began as an embarrassing draft. The creators were not more talented at first attempts; they were simply more willing to have a first attempt at all.
Judging a draft by finished-work standards is a category error — like criticising scaffolding for not being a house. The draft's only job is to exist so you have something real to improve.

body.heading: Lower the bar on purpose
paragraphs: Set a deliberately low target for first versions: “a messy page,” “the ugly sketch,” “the version where the song is just humming.” Some people even label the file BAD DRAFT 1, which makes its roughness official and oddly freeing.
Revision is where quality is made, and revision is a far kinder process than creation-from-nothing. You cannot edit a blank page — so make the non-blank page first, however badly.

takeaway: Let the first draft be bad. Editing needs material, not perfection.
